speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome, I understand you are presenting with hematuria and right flank pain. To help me determine the cause, could you describe the exact nature of the pain, such as whether it is sharp, colicky, or constant, and if it radiates to your groin?

Have you noticed any fever, chills, nausea, or vomiting accompanying these symptoms?

Do you have a history of kidney stones, recent urinary tract infections, or any recent trauma to your side or back?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Nephrolithiasis (Right Kidney Stone)

Based on your age, visible hematuria, right flank pain, and history of recurrent UTIs, the most likely cause is a kidney stone. Since you denied trauma, this is consistent with stone passage causing irritation. Would you like me to request a non-contrast CT of the abdomen/pelvis to confirm the presence and location of any stones?
